 Exposure to Active Directory, RDS, and Manhattan WMS 
 
 
 6 month full time contract in Altona North location - 5 days on-site  
 
 $60,000 + Superannuation pa. (prorated over 6 months)  
 
 
   Accelerate Your IT Career in Enterprise Supply Chain Operations  
 Step into an active operational environment supporting key systems, network infrastructure, and enterprise applications. This 6 month full time contract position sits within a premier national distribution enterprise based in Altona North. Reporting to the Technical Services Manager, you will serve as the first point of contact for technical resolution across corporate offices, retail channels, and high volume distribution facilities. 
  The Role  You will own the day to day ticket lifecycle through Freshdesk, triaging and resolving Level 1 support requests within defined service level agreements. This position delivers broad technical exposure, ranging from endpoint hardware configuration to user session management and enterprise application troubleshooting. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 
 Managing Active Directory user accounts, access permissions, and group policies. 
 
 
 Resolving Remote Desktop Services (RDS) user session disconnects and connectivity issues. 
 
 
 Troubleshooting local network connectivity (LAN/Wi-Fi) and maintaining network printer infrastructure. 
 
 
 Delivering end user PC support, including device setup, imaging, and software installation. 
 
 
 Supporting core enterprise tools, including Sage 300/Accpac ERP and Manhattan Scale Warehouse Management System (WMS). 
 
 
 Building internal knowledge base documentation by recording recurring issues and standard resolutions. 
 
 
   The Tech Stack & Environment  
 
 
  Identity & Access:  Active Directory 
 
 
  Remote Access:  Remote Desktop Services (RDS) 
 
 
  Ticketing & Service Desk:  Freshdesk 
 
 
  Enterprise Applications:  Sage 300 / Accpac, Microsoft Dynamics 365 CE/BC 
 
 
  Supply Chain Tech:  Manhattan Scale WMS, thermal network printers, barcode endpoints 
 
 
  Database & Diagnostic Tools:  Microsoft SQL (basic query execution) 
 
 
   What You'll Bring  
 
 
 Demonstrated track record in a Level 1 application or technical helpdesk role. 
 
 
 Practical experience administering Active Directory user accounts and permissions. 
 
 
 Familiarity supporting Remote Desktop Services (RDS) environments. 
 
 
 Exposure to ERP platforms (Sage 300/Accpac) or Warehouse Management Systems (Manhattan Scale) highly regarded. 
 
 
 Strong endpoint troubleshooting skills across PC hardware, software, and local network setups. 
 
 
 Calm, customer focused communication style with structured ticket logging discipline. 
 
 
 Full working rights in Australia for the duration of the 6 month term.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

About the role

We are looking for a special kind of person - a St Vincent's kind of person. Someone who puts compassion, connection and caring for other people at the heart of everything they do.
 

As a Hotel Services Assistant - Environmental Services Assistant, you will be joining our dynamic team at St Vincent's Care Corinda in Food Services, Laundry as well as Cleaning space. In this role you provide services that support effective and high quality cleaning outcomes for residents and customers of the aged care home. You will provide high quality food services and support residents with their food choices, ensuring residents feel valued, respected and engaged. You are also responsible for assisting the kitchen team to deliver quality meals in a timely manner and ensuring that the kitchen is hygienic, safe and operational, while maintaining the St Vincent's Care Services Policy around meals and dining experience. All positions contribute to the provision of quality and sustainable health services within the ethos of the philosophy, mission, values and ethics of the St Vincent's Health Australia.

What's on your CV is important, but what's in your heart matters more.
Because at St Vincent's, kindness works for us.

For further information on our brand new facility please visit www.svcs.org.au-corinda

Things that work for us:

Certificate in Hospitality and Kitchen Management (or other relevant qualification)

Relevant experience in similar field and experience in working with Dementia clients would be an advantage

Ability to work on a casual basis AM and PM shifts

Experience with Housekeeping and Food Services area including meal preparation, presentation, and distribution; Caf Service

Capable of assisting residents with laundry, putting clothes away, and general household tasks including cleaning

Comfortable developing a relationship with each resident in your care, building trust and familiarity and supporting everyone's personal space to be homelike, respectful and safe

Strong attention to detail and excellent communication skills

High level of customer service skills

Know, understand, and adhere to the requirements of the Aged Care Quality Standards and Food Safety standards

Ability to follow directives as per care plan

Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC)
 

Things that work for you:

Competitive salary packaging options up to $15,990, Novated leasing, plus an optional Meals and Entertainment card up to $2,650 per annum

Opportunity to work for the nation's largest Catholic not-for-profit health and aged care provider, with a rapidly growing and progressive vision

Friendly team environment with a great community care spirit

Ability to visibly see your impact on the business and its service

No cost uniforms and training

Free annual flu vaccination

No mandatory COVID vaccination

Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families

Access to the Fitness Passport (FP)

Why become part of the St Vincent's Care family?

Because you're like us, you believe that every act of kindness makes the world a better place. Better for everyone who lives in the 20+ facilities and locations we operate in Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. Better for all our staff and employees, who work tirelessly to provide the highest levels of care and quality of life for our clients. And better support for the local communities we play an important role in and continue to support.
 

For more than 175 years, St Vincent's Care Services (SVCS) has been a leading Catholic provider of Aged Care Services in Australia and the legacy of compassion, justice, integrity and excellence entrusted to us by the Sisters of Charity and their Founder Mary Aitkenhead continues to inspire our work today. Our spiritual and hospital-based heritage has taught us that wellness is about more than medical needs. It's about building a true partnership around trust and respect. That's why we take a person-centred approach - delivering holistic, individual care that achieves wellbeing for mind, body and spirit. At St Vincent's we value inclusivity and diversity and acknowledge the important of creating a work environment that is welcome, safe, fair and impartial and invite people from all backgrounds to join our caring family.

Reconciliation Action Plan

St Vincent's Health Australia embraces Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people's unique perspectives, knowledge, and cultural. We strive to achieve better physical, mental, and spiritual health outcomes through continued connection with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. We understand the need to effectively engage with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities to influence decision making at all levels and to create opportunity through sustainable and culturally safe employment.

As an experienced service operations leader, ideally within aged care, healthcare, or a similar environment, you'll be self-motivated, proactive, and bring strong leadership capability. You'll empower your team to deliver safe, high-quality, person-centred services, while reinforcing the importance of food safety, compliance, and continuous improvement. You'll demonstrate: 

Strong knowledge of food safety, infection control, and service standards, supported by experience in a regulated environment

Experience leading teams across kitchen operations, cleaning and-or laundry services

Proven leadership capability, including coaching, rostering, and building a positive team culture 

A proactive approach to problem-solving, organisation, and continuous improvement 

Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage with residents, families, and stakeholders 

Essential qualifications & licences: 

Certificate IV in Leadership & Management (or Diploma) 

A relevant trade or operational qualification (e.g. Certificate IV in Hospitality, Commercial Cookery or similar), or equivalent supervisory experience 

Food Safety Supervisor Certification

Ability to satisfy all required probity checks in line with legislation and BlueCare policies 

Employee Benefits: 

Save tax and increase your take home pay by salary packaging your everyday living expenses and bills (up to $15,900) and meal entertainment (up to $2,650) per annum 

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs 

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months service, in addition to the government scheme 

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events 

Career development opportunities with one of the most trusted community and residential care providers in Australia to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

BlueCare is proudly part of the UnitingCare Family, we'd love you to be too

Joining the state's largest network of aged care workers with its over 8,000 strong, bright team in blue, you'll also be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. With more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, you are part of something bigger. Our team are compassionate, inclusive and committed to the work we do, helping people live life in all its fullness.

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

Provide welcoming, safe & nurturing services for children 

Implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services

Appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

Abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple -everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. For additional support and to meet our RAP Team, email reconciliation@ucareqld.com.au

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety.

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. About the Business:
Pakenham Radiators and Mechanical Services Pty Ltd is a well-established automotive workshop specialising in radiator repairs, recoring, flushes, assemblies and custom builds, while also delivering comprehensive mechanical services including logbook servicing, general repairs and air conditioning re-gas and repairs. Serving the local Pakenham community, the business is known for its technical expertise, modern equipment and strong focus on quality workmanship and customer satisfaction, ensuring every vehicle leaves the workshop performing safely and reliably.
About the Position:
The Motor Mechanic role is central to the workshop’s day-to-day operations, responsible for accurately diagnosing vehicle faults, performing high-quality repairs and maintenance, and ensuring vehicles are returned to customers in optimal condition. This position plays a key part in upholding the business’s reputation for reliable automotive service and supporting efficient workshop throughput.
Key Responsibilities:
Diagnose vehicles by mechanical testing and observation
Provide detailed estimates of repairs and replacements
Repair and replace diagnosed issues
Conduct routine maintenance and service aiming to vehicle functionality and longevity
Test drive vehicles after repairs to ensure complete repair work is performed
File appropriate documentation on service and repair works completed
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate IV or higher trade qualifications.
Minimum 3 years of work experience; experience in radiator repair preferred.
Highly motivated with the ability to work autonomously, strong technical diagnostic and repair skills, and a demonstrated commitment to excellent customer service.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
